title: Noncrossing Two-Nearest-Predecessor Orders on Nearly Circular Ellipses
abstract: We prove a uniform all-cardinality existence theorem for noncrossing chronological two-nearest-predecessor graphs on sufficiently near-circular ellipses. Put R = sqrt(2/sin(2*pi/5) - 1). For every ellipse with semiaxes a >= b > 0 and a/b <= R, and every finite set of at least three distinct boundary sites, there is an order starting with a triangle in which every subsequent site is joined to exactly its two Euclidean-nearest earlier sites. All edges persist, and no two independent edges properly cross. Cartesian-lexicographic order resolves equal-distance predecessor ties. The sufficient ratio bound includes equality, all finite cardinalities and arbitrarily close distinct sites. The interest lies in planarity despite compulsory distance-ranked edges: unlike conventional convex-polygon triangulation, the two incoming edges cannot be chosen just to avoid crossings. The constructive proof uses recursive metric-ear deletion; the accompanying manuscript also gives an exact-real comparison-model algorithm, whose complexity is not a separately compared Lean claim. The bound is not claimed to be sharp; historical priority remains unestablished. The repository also contains formally proved supporting geometry and a concrete noncircular corollary, but these are not submitted as independent research results in the selected Comparator configuration.
